title: Pre AI SAT MBA
subtitle: Non-Tech AI SAT (Management) Benchmark Assessment
instructions: This assessment measures practical AI literacy, prompt engineering, evaluation judgment, and management workflow readiness.
There are 10 self-perception rating items followed by 40 scenario and concept multiple-choice questions.
Answer based on practical business judgment. There is no negative marking.
Your responses are saved continuously in real time.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-01
questions.prompt: I can explain in plain terms why an AI tool sometimes gives a confidently wrong answer.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-02
questions.prompt: I understand why an AI assistant can lose track of something said earlier in a long conversation.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-03
questions.prompt: I can tell a colleague what limits how much text an AI tool can ‘see’ at once.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-04
questions.prompt: I can get noticeably better output from an AI tool just by rewriting how I ask for it.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-05
questions.prompt: I can give an AI tool examples of what I want so it copies the pattern correctly.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-06
questions.prompt: When an AI's first answer misses the mark, I know how to guide it toward what I actually need across a few follow-up messages.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-07
questions.prompt: Before I act on something an AI tool tells me, I check whether it's actually true.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-08
questions.prompt: I can get an AI tool to pull together information from multiple sources into one clear summary.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-09
questions.prompt: I can tell when an AI-generated answer is guessing versus when it's grounded in something real.

questions.title: Perception Check · PC-10
questions.prompt: I would catch it if an AI assistant made up a policy or price that isn't real.

questions.title: AI Literacy · Q1
questions.prompt: A colleague pastes a 40-page document into an AI chat and the tool suddenly ‘forgets’ the details from the first ten pages. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The AI only reads the last page
The document exceeded the tool's context window
The AI is deliberately hiding information

questions.title: AI Literacy · Q2
questions.prompt: An AI assistant confidently states a statistic that turns out to be completely fabricated. What is this called?

questions.title: AI Literacy · Q3
questions.prompt: What is a ‘token’ in the context of how an AI language model processes text?

options.text: A unit of text (roughly a word piece) the model processes

questions.title: AI Literacy · Q4
questions.prompt: Why might an AI tool give a different answer to the same question asked twice?

options.text: Language models generate responses with some built-in variability
It only works once per session

questions.title: AI Literacy · Q5
questions.prompt: A team member says ‘the AI just knows everything.’ What is the most accurate correction?

options.text: It generates plausible responses based on patterns in training data, which can be wrong or outdated
It only knows what's on the internet today
It has to be connected to a database to know anything
It has real-time access to all information

questions.title: Prompt Engineering · Q1
questions.prompt: A team wants an AI tool to categorize incoming support tickets into ‘Billing,’ ‘Technical,’ or ‘General’ exactly the way they've been doing it manually. What's the best prompting approach?
questions.explanationHint: Few-shot fits pattern-matching against existing examples.

options.text: Multi-turn: split the task across many separate messages
Zero-shot: just ask it to categorize
Negative prompting: only tell it what not to do
Few-shot: give 3-4 labeled examples of tickets and their correct category, then ask it to continue the pattern

questions.title: Prompt Engineering · Q2
questions.prompt: A finance team needs an AI tool to work through a multi-step reimbursement calculation without skipping steps. Which technique best fits?
questions.explanationHint: CoT reduces skipped steps in multi-step reasoning.

options.text: Chain-of-thought: ask the model to reason step-by-step before giving the final number

questions.title: Prompt Engineering · Q3
questions.prompt: A marketing manager wants AI-generated copy to sound like it's written by a 10-year veteran brand strategist, not a generic assistant. Best technique?

options.text: Role/context prompting: assign the AI a persona and background before the task

questions.title: Prompt Engineering · Q4
questions.prompt: A restaurant wants AI-drafted reservation confirmations that never mention pricing or discounts. What should the prompt include?

options.text: A request for a longer response
A single example with no instructions
An explicit instruction stating what the AI must not mention (e.g., pricing, discounts)
A long list of what to include

questions.title: Prompt Engineering · Q5
questions.prompt: A recruiter is refining a job description with an AI tool: first draft, then narrowing the tone, then trimming length. This is an example of:
questions.explanationHint: Iterative refinement across messages defines multi-turn.

options.text: Multi-turn prompting: iterating across several connected messages toward a refined result

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval · Q1
questions.prompt: An AI tool summarizes three articles into one brief but the summary includes a claim not found in any of them. What should the user do?

options.text: Assume the AI found a fourth uncited source
Trust it since AI tools are usually accurate
Ignore it since summaries are always safe
Verify the claim against the original sources before using it

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval · Q2
questions.prompt: What is the best first step when an AI-generated answer is needed for a decision with real financial consequences?

options.text: Assume it's correct if it sounds confident
Ask the AI to repeat the answer twice
Cross-check the answer against at least one independent, trusted source

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval · Q3
questions.prompt: A vague search query like ‘best tool’ returns unhelpful AI results. What's the best fix?

options.text: Narrow the query with specific criteria (use case, budget, constraints)
Give up and search manually only

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval · Q4
questions.prompt: Which is a red flag that an AI-retrieved ‘fact’ may be unreliable?

options.text: It cannot be traced to any verifiable source when checked

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval · Q5
questions.prompt: When asking an AI tool to compare pricing across competitors, what's the safest practice?

options.text: Treat the figures as a starting point and verify current pricing directly with each source

questions.title: Responsible AI · Q1
questions.prompt: A customer chatbot's system prompt has no instruction about what to do when asked something outside its scope. What's the most likely failure?

options.text: It may confidently answer questions it shouldn't, including inventing information

questions.title: Responsible AI · Q2
questions.prompt: A support bot is asked about a refund policy that doesn't exist in its training. Without proper guardrails, what's the biggest risk?

options.text: It may invent a plausible-sounding but false policy

questions.title: Responsible AI · Q3
questions.prompt: What should a well-designed system prompt include for a customer-facing AI agent handling pricing questions?

options.text: An explicit instruction to only state verified pricing and escalate anything uncertain
Freedom to estimate prices when unsure
A joke to lighten the mood

questions.title: Responsible AI · Q4
questions.prompt: A chatbot handling account changes has no escalation rule for sensitive requests (e.g., closing an account). What should be added?

options.text: A rule to always approve the request
Nothing, the bot should handle everything itself
A rule requiring escalation to a human for sensitive or high-stakes actions
A rule to always deny the request

questions.title: Responsible AI · Q5
questions.prompt: Why is ‘scope’ an important element of a responsible AI system prompt?

options.text: It defines what the AI is and isn't allowed to address, preventing it from overstepping into risky territory
It's only relevant for legal teams

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement · Q1
questions.prompt: Two AI-generated marketing emails are shown. Email A is polished but factually vague; Email B is less polished but factually precise and actionable. For a campaign requiring accuracy, which should be preferred?

options.text: Email B, because factual precision matters more for the stated goal
Email A, because polish matters most

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement · Q2
questions.prompt: What's the first question to ask when evaluating any AI-generated output before using it?

options.text: Did it take a long time to generate?
Does it actually meet the task's real requirements and constraints?

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement · Q3
questions.prompt: An AI-written report reads smoothly but contains a factual contradiction between two sections. What should a careful reviewer do?

options.text: Flag and resolve the contradiction before using the report
Shorten the report to hide the issue
Ignore it since it reads well

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement · Q4
questions.prompt: When comparing two AI outputs for the same task, which is the most reliable evaluation method?

options.text: Checking each against explicit, pre-defined criteria relevant to the task

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement · Q5
questions.prompt: An AI-generated code snippet runs without errors. Does that guarantee it's correct?

options.text: Yes, no errors means it's fully correct
No, it should still be checked against the actual requirement, since it can run without producing the right result

questions.title: AI Content Creation · Q1
questions.prompt: An AI content flow is supposed to output a caption and a separate list of hashtags as two distinct fields, but instead returns one blended paragraph with hashtags mixed into the caption text. What's the defect?

options.text: The structured-output separation between caption and hashtags has broken down

questions.title: AI Content Creation · Q2
questions.prompt: A content generation flow is meant to output JSON with fields ‘caption’ and ‘hashtags’ but instead returns plain unstructured text. What will most likely happen downstream?

options.text: Systems expecting structured fields will fail to parse or post correctly
It has no effect on automation
Nothing, downstream systems handle any format

questions.title: AI Content Creation · Q3
questions.prompt: A caption-generation prompt is expected to produce content matching brand voice, but output reads generic and could belong to any brand. What's the most direct fix?

options.text: Add explicit brand-voice examples or descriptors (tone, phrases, audience) to the prompt

questions.title: AI Content Creation · Q4
questions.prompt: An Instagram post flow generates a caption and, separately, an image-generation prompt. A reviewer notices the image prompt describes something unrelated to the caption's topic. What's the defect?

options.text: A break in the caption/image-prompt alignment — the two outputs should describe the same underlying content

questions.title: AI Content Creation · Q5
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of separating ‘caption’ and ‘hashtags’ into distinct structured fields rather than one blob of text?

options.text: It lets downstream systems (posting tools, scheduling automation) reliably extract and use each part correctly

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt · Q1
questions.prompt: A team has a working AI-assisted design mockup for a customer-facing tool but no backend workflow built yet. What's the correct next step?

options.text: Start over with a new design
Build the workflow that actually powers the design before treating it as done

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt · Q2
questions.prompt: A team has built an automation workflow but has no interface for anyone to actually use it. What's missing?

options.text: A frontend or interface layer connecting users to the workflow
Nothing, the workflow alone is sufficient

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt · Q3
questions.prompt: What is the benefit of using a persistent AI ‘project’ space (with saved context/files) over starting a fresh chat every time for related work?

options.text: It removes the need for review
It retains relevant background so the AI doesn't need to be re-briefed each time, saving effort
No benefit, fresh chats are always better

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt · Q4
questions.prompt: A team keeps re-explaining the same background information to an AI tool in every new conversation. What productivity practice would fix this?

options.text: Keep repeating it — there's no alternative
Use a different AI tool each time
Set up a persistent project or reusable context/skill so the background is available automatically

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt · Q5
questions.prompt: What's the correct build order when a team has a validated idea but nothing built yet, following a design-to-workflow-to-app sequence?

options.text: Build the frontend first, then the workflow, then the design
Skip design and workflow, go straight to launch
Build all three simultaneously with no sequence
Start with the design, then build the workflow it depends on, then connect the frontend/app layer

questions.title: AI Workflow Automation · Q1
questions.prompt: A support automation has a trigger and an AI agent step, but the agent generates its reply as plain text instead of calling the defined send-message tool. What's the defect?

options.text: No defect, plain text is fine
The agent isn't using its available tool to actually deliver the message, so the reply likely never reaches the customer

questions.title: AI Workflow Automation · Q2
questions.prompt: A chatbot flow has no memory component, so it treats every message in a conversation as if it's the first. What's the resulting problem?

options.text: It automatically fixes itself over time
The bot can't maintain context across a multi-message conversation, leading to repeated questions or disjointed replies
No problem, this is more efficient

questions.title: AI Workflow Automation · Q3
questions.prompt: An automated flow is triggered whenever a message arrives, but the flow has no rule for what happens if the AI agent isn't confident in its answer. What's missing?

options.text: An escalation or fallback path for low-confidence or out-of-scope situations

questions.title: Agentic AI · Q1
questions.prompt: What distinguishes an ‘agentic’ flow from a simple linear automation?

options.text: An agentic flow includes a decision-making step where the AI determines the next action rather than following a fixed sequence

questions.title: Agentic AI · Q2
questions.prompt: A campaign needs both a caption and an image brief produced together for every post, at volume. Why does running these as one coordinated flow (rather than one after another) improve throughput?

options.text: It only works for a single post
It doesn't — sequential is always faster
Coordinated (parallel) generation with shared context avoids duplicated setup and keeps both outputs aligned without waiting on each other unnecessarily
It removes the need for either output
